data.title: PIMCO: AI debt and refinancing stress are splitting the corporate bond market in two
data.description:
The split points to rising default and restructuring risk among CCC-rated borrowers, particularly in technology, media, telecoms and consumer sectors, even without a recession. That's a warning for holders of lower-quality junk debt and for leveraged loan markets. In investment grade, heavy AI issuance from hyperscalers is likely to keep pressure on top-rated tech bonds, while scarce non-AI credit stays in demand. The trend also ties AI's financing needs more closely to bond-market conditions: if issuance slows after the midterms, AA spreads could recover. A sharper economic slowdown is the main risk, since investment grade spreads can widen quickly once growth fears take hold.

---

data.title: Gold's road back to $5,000: four big banks bet on recovery, but the Fed sets the pace
data.description:
The banks' common message is that gold's direction in the coming months depends on the Fed, not on geopolitics. Throughout the Iran war, higher oil has fed rate-hike expectations and weighed on bullion. That makes upcoming US inflation data and the December Fed decision the key near-term drivers, with any signs of a peak in tightening likely to bring dip buyers back. Oil is the swing risk: BofA's stress case shows a renewed energy spike could keep gold under pressure well into 2027. Central bank buying, which Goldman estimates at around 60 tonnes a month, is the main floor beneath prices.

---

data.title: BlackRock says markets overprice Fed hikes, sees two not three as energy shock fades
data.description:
BlackRock's view runs against Monday's hawkish Fed commentary and against market pricing, so the October PCE data becomes a key test. A softer services reading would back BlackRock and could pull Fed pricing toward two hikes, supporting short-dated Treasuries and easing some pressure on the US dollar. For oil, BlackRock's case depends on the recent sharp fall in crude and fuel prices holding. A renewed rise in energy costs would undercut its view and strengthen the case for more Fed tightening. Its expectation of an ECB hike next month, with more depending on energy pass-through, points to tighter policy in Europe than the US for longer.

data.title: Analysts cheer Huang's Nvidia return but question the board's sudden U-turn
data.description:
For investors, the reaction splits into two trades: relief that Nvidia's strategy and customer relationships stay intact, and a new governance discount tied to the board's credibility. The valuation argument, with shares at around 11 times forward earnings according to one fund manager, gives the rebound fundamental support beyond sentiment. Political risk is now a bigger factor in AI stocks after the midterm results, with regulation and limits on data centre development seen as the main threats to the infrastructure build-out. Any board changes or developments in the ongoing investigations could quickly test Monday's rally.

---

data.title: Singapore sees AI boom carrying 2026, but slower AI investment growth to weigh on 2027
data.description:
Coming from one of the region's biggest AI winners, the comments are an early official signal that growth in AI capital spending may peak in 2026. That matters for chip and electronics supply chains across Taiwan, Korea and Japan. Markets are likely to read it as a slowdown in the rate of growth rather than a contraction, so there's limited near-term risk for AI-linked equities. Still, it adds to the debate over 2027 earnings expectations for the sector. For the Singapore dollar, firm near-term growth supports the MAS keeping its current settings in January, while the softer 2027 outlook limits the case for any further tightening.

---

data.title: Bank of Korea seen hiking to 3.25% this week, with one final move in early 2027
data.description:
With a hike fully priced, the reaction on Thursday will depend on the BOK's guidance. A signal that the next move is the last would support the 3.50% peak view and could weigh lightly on the won, while an open-ended tone would push Korean bond yields higher. The won's 7% gain this year gives the BOK room to stay measured, but a run of Fed hikes would test that. Korean equities, already at 10-month lows after last week's tech sell-off, face the double hit of higher borrowing costs and fragile sentiment, though the semiconductor export story remains supportive for chipmakers.

---

data.title: Singapore Q3 GDP jumps 6.1%, growth forecast lifted to around 6% as exports boom
data.description:
The upgrade supports the Singapore dollar and reduces any pressure on the Monetary Authority of Singapore to ease at its January review, since stronger growth argues for keeping current settings. For the region, the 30%-32% NODX forecast is a strong signal of continued AI-related electronics demand. That's positive for chip and electronics supply chains in Taiwan, Korea and Malaysia, and it comes the morning after the Nvidia-led rebound in tech stocks. The 2027 range of 2.5% to 4.5% is a reminder that the boom is expected to fade. New US licensing rules on advanced AI chip shipments through Singapore are a risk to watch for the trade hub.

---

data.title: Goldman says AI's next test is proving the economics, not the technology
data.description:
Goldman's focus on financing favours companies with strong balance sheets and reliable access to capital, which could widen the valuation gap between cash-rich hyperscalers and highly leveraged AI builders. Its view that agentic AI could push computing demand beyond user growth supports the chip, memory and power supply chain, consistent with its earlier note on AI spending broadening beyond Nvidia. Its expectation that permit and power constraints will shift where capacity is built, not reduce it, points to rising demand for sites with available energy, a theme relevant to utilities and energy markets. For newly listed AI names, the note's emphasis on execution suggests trading will stay sensitive to revenue updates.

---

data.title: Fed's Williams won't rule out back-to-back rate hikes as data drives the path
data.description:
The openness to consecutive hikes adds upside risk to Fed pricing beyond December, with traders more likely to build in a follow-up move in early 2027. That should keep short-dated Treasury yields supported and give the US dollar a firmer floor, especially against currencies whose central banks are moving toward cuts. For equities, Williams set a high bar for market weakness to change his view, which limits hopes that renewed tech volatility would slow the Fed. Energy remains central to his inflation outlook, so any rise in oil prices would add weight to the case for a faster pace of hikes.

---

data.title: ANZ pulls first RBA rate cut forward to June 2027, sees three cuts by early 2028
data.description:
The bigger story for currency markets is the policy divergence. The RBA is now widely expected to start easing in mid-2027, while the Fed is still on a hiking path, with a December increase broadly expected. A narrowing rate gap between the two would weigh on the Australian dollar against the US dollar over time. Short-dated Australian rates may see limited reaction, because markets had already priced a June cut as more likely than not after the jobs data. The effect is more likely to show up further out on the curve. Any upside surprise in quarterly inflation would test ANZ's call quickly and could prompt a sharp repricing back toward a later start to easing.

---

data.title: Tokyo gets its first look at the Nvidia whiplash as Asia trades the Huang rebound
data.description:
Asian chip stocks get their first full chance today to respond to Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as chief executive, and the setup differs sharply from market to market.

Tokyo is the clearest case. Japanese markets were shut on Monday for a public holiday, so today's session is the first since Friday's AI-led sell-off on Wall Street and Monday's sharp rebound, when the Nasdaq Composite jumped 6.5%. Chip equipment and testing names with close ties to the AI supply chain, such as Advantest and Tokyo Electron, will be the ones to watch.

data.title: Goldman sees up to $15 trillion for AI infrastructure as spending spreads beyond Nvidia
data.description:
Goldman's framing favours the bottleneck parts of the AI supply chain, particularly memory makers, advanced packaging specialists and power infrastructure, over a single-stock bet on Nvidia. That is relevant for Asian equities, where memory and packaging exposure is concentrated in Korea and Taiwan. The view that neocloud lending now depends on milestones should ease some credit concerns around the sector, although it also implies slower, more conditional build-outs. The power angle ties AI spending to energy and utilities demand, a theme that is likely to keep electricity infrastructure in focus as data centre construction grows.

data.title: Fed's Williams pins inflation on unusual factors, sees 2027 bringing it lower
data.description:
The Q&A softens the tone of Williams' prepared remarks without changing their core message, so pricing for a quarter-point hike on December 9 is unlikely to move much. His focus on unusual factors puts energy back at the centre. Brent is still around $92, well above the roughly $72 seen in late February before the US war with Iran began, so oil remains the main factor in how quickly 2027 delivers the lower inflation he expects. A sustained fall in crude would strengthen the case for a shallower hiking path next year, while fresh supply disruption would push the other way. His caution on hiring matters for the US dollar, since any slowdown in payrolls would weaken the case for further increases beyond December.

data.title: Nvidia's Huang is back. Monday's rally leaves three big questions unanswered.
data.description:
Asia gets the first real test today of whether the relief extends beyond US chipmakers: Tokyo reopens after a holiday, and Seoul's memory makers sold off before the news broke. In rates, a firmer equity backdrop gives the Fed cover to raise rates in December, which should keep short-dated Treasury yields supported and limit any pullback in the US dollar. Energy shares lagged during the rebound, which suggests the money returning to AI did not spill over into commodity-linked sectors. Nvidia volatility is likely to stay elevated into the December 1 congressional interview, since the stock now prices in a clean resolution of the security questions.

--

data.title: Jensen Huang is back in charge.  Nvidia moves higher.
data.description:
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite had their best day since April 9, 2025, as buyers returned to beaten-down AI and chip stocks. Nvidia led the rebound, jumping $39.52 to $165.05 after its board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. The Nasdaq 100 gained 6.86%, the biggest move among the major US indices, while the Dow added more than 1,448 points.

The buying spread well beyond Nvidia. The Russell 2000 rose 3.40%, 26 of the 30 Dow stocks advanced, and S&P 500 gainers outnumbered decliners 406 to 79. Both Nasdaq indices recovered all of Friday’s losses, and the S&P 500 snapped a seven-session losing streak. The four major indices with reported intraday ranges stayed positive throughout the session and each held more than 84% of its peak point gain into the close. images.investinglive.com
